brief.headline: Bank Nifty Leads Domestic Rally; Global Markets Face Tech-Led Selloff
brief.summary: Indian equities closed higher led by strong banking and healthcare gains, with Nifty 50 reaching 25800.6 and Bank Nifty gaining 2.49%. However, global markets face severe headwinds as the Nasdaq dropped 5.28% in its worst week since 2020 amid AI stock volatility. Domestic cues, foreign portfolio investor flows, and crude oil prices will dictate momentum in the upcoming holiday-shortened week.

takeaways.text: Banking and hospital stocks drove Indian markets higher, with Nifty Bank rising around 16% month-to-date and hospital stocks rallying up to 14%.
India's net oil and gas import bill rose 60% year-on-year to $16 billion in October as Brent crude prices nearly doubled.
US markets suffered sharp losses with Nasdaq falling 5.28% and S&P 500 dropping 3.70% as tech selloff weighed on equities.
China lowered stock financing margin requirements to 80% to boost equity market liquidity after leveraged trading activity declined.
Amazon is closing in on a $7.5bn deal to buy AI startup Decart to boost AWS computing power.
California's probe into Nvidia covers potential criminal law violations regarding chip sales to China and investor disclosure.

sections.india: Nifty 50 gained 1.12% to close at 25800.6, while Bank Nifty rallied 2.49% to 64635.2 led by strong gains across private and PSU banks. Motilal Oswal Financial Services expects corporate earnings to remain upbeat for second half of FY27 on healthy demand and order pipelines. India's oil and gas import bill surged 60% year-on-year to $16 billion in October due to higher crude prices.
sections.world: Global markets experienced heavy selling as Nasdaq dropped 5.28% and Dow Jones lost 1.93%, with S&P 500 entering correction territory. China reduced its margin requirement to 80% to bolster liquidity in its equity markets. Brent Crude eased 2.21% to 89.95, while Gold fell 4.62% to 3515.4.
sections.tech: Anthropic completed its historic Nasdaq debut, though broader tech sentiment remains pressured by Nvidia volatility and regulatory scrutiny. California expanded its investigation into Nvidia to cover potential criminal law violations over chip sales to China. Meanwhile, Amazon is nearing a $7.5bn acquisition of AI startup Decart.
